findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pads with locations in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas of the site. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1 transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" near Building 1. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains legend symbols for transformer pads but no actual transformer pads are drawn on the plan. Sheets 11 (Grading Plan), 12 (Storm Sewer Plan), and 31 (Landscape Plan) do not show any transformer locations. This creates significant inconsistency: 4 transformers are documented on the electrical plan but only 1 appears on the main site plan, and transformers are entirely absent from the wet utilities, grading, storm, and landscape plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that georeferenced AutoCAD drawings clearly delineate electrical infrastructure locations across all required plan sheets. The standard sheet set for transformer documentation includes site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading/storm plans when applicable. The variance between sheets—with Sheet 21 showing 4 transformers and Sheet 9 showing only 1—indicates either incomplete documentation on the site plan or an incomplete electrical design on Sheet 21. The complete absence of transformers from Sheets 19, 31, 11, and 12 prevents verification of clearances, conflicts with other utilities, and tree preservation impacts. For a multi-building development with 4 transformers, omitting transformers from landscape and grading plans prevents the reviewer from verifying required clearances and access routes.
findings.comment: Transformer locations are not shown consistently across all required plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads, Sheet 9 shows 1 transformer, and Sheets 11, 12, 19, and 31 show no transformers. Add transformer locations to site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan. Ensure all transformer locations are consistent across all sheets.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 electrical plan labels all transformer locations uniformly as "Electrical Transformer Pad" with no supplemental callouts, notes, or specifications indicating the type of transformer. The label alone provides no information to distinguish between pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault, or service drop configurations. No notes on the electrical plan specify transformer type for the site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly delineate electrical infrastructure with sufficient detail for Austin Energy to verify that the proposed service configuration meets code requirements. Transformer type is fundamental information: pad-mounted transformers require specific clearances per UCM § 1.10.4; vault installations must demonstrate conformance with niche design requirements and Network Area restrictions (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3); pole-mounted units have different access and safety requirements. Omitting type designation prevents verification of compliance with clearance and placement standards.
findings.comment: Transformer type not specified. Each transformer pad must be labeled with its specific type: pad-mounted, pole-mounted, vault, or service drop. Add callout notes or legend entries identifying the type for each transformer on the electrical plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 depicts 4 transformer pads: one in the northwest area (west of Buildings 1 and 2), one in the southwest area (west of Building 8), one in the northeast central area (east of Building 4), and one in the southeast central area (east of Building 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts only 1 transformer pad labeled "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" located near Building 1 (northwest area). The three transformers shown on Sheet 21 (southwest, northeast, southeast) are entirely absent from Sheet 9.
findings.reasoning: Transformer locations on Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) show 4 transformer pads, but Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows only 1. This discrepancy violates the requirement for consistent documentation across plan sheets. Reconcile the transformer count and locations between sheets. Ensure all proposed transformers are shown on both the main site plan and the electrical design plan, with matching locations.
findings.comment: Transformer locations are not consistent across plan sheets. Sheet 21 shows 4 transformer pads while Sheet 9 shows only 1 transformer. Reconcile transformer locations and ensure all transformers appear on all required plan sheets with consistent positioning.

findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show any transformer pad locations, electrical routing, or transformer access areas. The landscape plan contains only landscape elements (proposed paving, street yards, parking lot landscaping, trees, irrigation system) and overhead electric line notation on the property boundary. The proposed planting plan—which includes numerous trees and shrub locations throughout the site—cannot be verified against transformer clearance requirements because no transformer locations or routing are depicted on the landscape plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of any side of pad-mounted electric equipment and requires root barriers for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground equipment. The landscape plan is the primary document for tree locations and planting design. Without transformer routing shown on the landscape plan, the reviewer cannot verify compliance with tree clearance requirements, cannot confirm that proposed plantings don't conflict with transformer access door swings, and cannot assess root barrier requirements for trees near underground conduit. This omission prevents approval of the landscape plan.
findings.comment: Transformer routing not shown on landscape plan. Show all transformer pad locations and access routes on the landscape plan. Verify that no trees are planted within 10 feet lateral clearance from any transformer side or within access door swing areas. Indicate root barrier requirements for trees within 20 feet of underground electrical routing.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 4 transformer pad locations but does not show any dedicated electrical easement boundaries or polygons around the transformer facilities. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows existing electrical easements on property boundaries (labeled as "5' Electric Easement") but does not show proposed easements around transformer equipment. The grouping overview notes that electrical easements must be adequate to cover: (1) the physical location of facilities, (2) required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (ranging from 3-15 feet depending on equipment side), and (3) areas needed for construction, operation, maintenance, and access. No such easement polygons are depicted in the site plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.24 defines easements as property rights necessary to ensure safe construction, operation, maintenance, and access to electric facilities. UCM § 1.10.4 specifies varying clearance requirements: hot-stick use areas require 10-15 feet clearance; sides with controls require 5 feet clearance from fencing; sides without operators may be 3 feet from removable fencing. Each transformer requires an easement adequate to encompass all clearance zones and access areas. UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly show easement boundaries. The complete absence of transformer easement delineation prevents verification that property within the site is reserved for electrical facilities and that access for Austin Energy maintenance is protected.
findings.comment: Electrical easement around transformer facilities not shown or not adequate. Show dedicated easement boundaries around each transformer pad sufficient to cover: (1) the physical equipment location, (2) all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4 (10-15 feet depending on equipment side and access requirements), and (3) Austin Energy access and maintenance areas. Label easement with recording information or "to be dedicated" notation.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels transformers as "Electrical Transformer Pad" on the electrical plan. Sheet 9 labels one transformer as "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" on the site plan. Sheets 19, 31, 11, and 12 contain no transformer labels whatsoever because transformers are not depicted on these sheets. The irregular labeling, combined with the absence of transformers from required sheets, means that the reviewer cannot verify consistent identification of electrical infrastructure across the document set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that electrical infrastructure be clearly labeled on all required plan sheets. Consistent, informative labeling enables Austin Energy and the City to verify that all proposed equipment is accounted for and properly identified across all disciplines. The current labeling is inconsistent ("Electrical Transformer Pad" vs. "Transformer Pad (Typ.)") and incomplete (missing from landscape, wet utilities, grading, and storm plans). This prevents confident cross-reference of electrical equipment across the plan set.
findings.comment: Transformer labels missing on required sheets or inconsistent. Establish consistent labeling (e.g., "Electrical Transformer Pad - Type [X], Size [Y] kVA") and show transformers on all required sheets: site plan, wet utilities plan, landscape plan, and grading plan (where applicable). Use a standard notation on all sheets.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels all four transformer pads with the text "Electrical Transformer Pad" but provides no kVA size, capacity rating, phase configuration, or other specification. No notes on the sheet detail transformer sizes. The architectural and electrical load information that would determine required transformer capacity is not included in the site plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires sufficient plan detail for Austin Energy to verify that proposed service meets project requirements. Transformer size is essential information: it determines clearance requirements, cable sizing, cooling needs, and whether additional transformers are needed. Omitting size makes it impossible to verify that the four transformers are adequate to serve 39 residential units, or that sizing complies with Austin Energy design standards.
findings.comment: Transformer size not specified. Label each transformer with its capacity in kVA (e.g., "50 kVA", "100 kVA") and include transformer specifications (phase, voltage, cooling method) on the electrical plan. Confirm with Austin Energy that the total proposed transformer capacity is adequate to serve all 39 units.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels transformers only as "Electrical Transformer Pad" with no indication of metering method. The eight meter locations are labeled as "Electrical Meters" but no callout specifies whether each meter is CT metered or building metered, or whether meters are grouped per UCM § 1.9.3.4 requirements. Service distribution enclosure or wireway locations are not identified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that plans clearly detail service infrastructure. Metering method (CT metered at the transformer vs. building metered) affects meter placement, conductor sizing, and point-of-service configuration. For multi-unit developments, UCM § 1.9.3.4 requires that when two or more meters are served from one service connection, meters and disconnects must be grouped in a common location (meter bank/SDE) with specified clearances and line-of-sight requirements. Omitting metering method prevents verification of compliance with grouping and accessibility standards.
findings.comment: Transformer metering method not labeled. Specify for each transformer whether it is CT metered (with secondary meter locations) or building metered (with individual unit metering). If meters are grouped (served from one service connection), label the service distribution enclosure, wireway, and meter bank location with grouping notation and reference to UCM § 1.9.3.4.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) contains no utility legend. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) contains no utility legend defining transformer or meter symbols. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) contains a Legend in the top-right corner that defines two electrical symbols: "- E - Proposed Underground Electric" and "[Square symbol] Transformer Pad". However, on Sheet 19, neither of these symbols are actually drawn on the plan—the legend defines symbols that are not used. Sheets 11, 12, and 31 contain no transformer symbols or legends.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires plans to delineate proposed utilities clearly. A utility legend is the standard method for communicating utility symbols and line types. The absence of a consistent legend across the site plan set, combined with the fact that the legend on Sheet 19 defines symbols that are not actually used, violates the clarity requirement. Austin Energy and City reviewers expect a unified legend identifying all proposed electrical infrastructure (transformers, meters, underground lines, easements) with symbols consistently applied across all relevant sheets.
findings.comment: Transformers not delineated in legend as proposed utilities. Add a Utility Legend to the site plan, wet utilities plan, and electrical plan defining the symbols for: (1) Transformer Pad, (2) Proposed Underground Electric Line, (3) Electrical Meter, (4) Electrical Easement, and (5) Pull Box. Use consistent symbols across all sheets. Ensure symbols are actually applied on the plans.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows 8 meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" on building exterior walls. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one gas meter but does not show electrical meter locations. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has a legend entry for utility symbols but no meters are drawn on the plan. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does not show electrical meter locations. The required site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan all lack electrical meter documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.A requires meter locations to be shown on plans. Meters must be on first floor or ground level, readily accessible, within sight of the transformer, and for grouped metering, positioned with disconnects in a common location per UCM § 1.9.3.4. The absence of meter locations on the site plan and landscape plan prevents verification of accessibility, sightlines to transformers, and clearances from other utilities. For a multi-unit development, meter locations are essential to demonstrating that the metering and disconnection configuration complies with grouped metering requirements.
findings.comment: Meter locations not shown on all required plan sheets. Show all electrical meter locations on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. Identify each meter location with a callout and label. Note whether meters are grouped (per UCM § 1.9.3.4) or individual. Verify that each meter location is: (1) at ground level, (2) readily accessible, (3) within sight of its serving transformer, and (4) positioned with disconnects within 20 feet for grouped configurations.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 labels meters as "Electrical Meters" with callout lines to building wall locations. Sheets 9, 19, and 31 do not show meters or meter labels. No callouts define meter specifications, disconnect locations, service distribution enclosure locations, or grouping configurations. For a multi-unit residential development, disconnect locations are not identified relative to meters.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 and § 1.16.0 require that plans clearly identify meter and disconnect locations. Meter labels and disconnect callouts enable Austin Energy to verify that the service configuration is accessible, properly grouped (if applicable), and compliant with spacing requirements (maximum 20 feet between meter and disconnect per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Without labels and callouts on the site, wet utilities, and landscape plans, the reviewer cannot confirm that the metering design meets code requirements across all plan disciplines.
findings.comment: Meters and disconnects not labeled on all required sheets. Label all electrical meters and disconnects on the site plan, wet utilities plan, and landscape plan. For grouped metering, label the service distribution enclosure (SDE) and wireway location, and note the distance between meters and disconnects (maximum 20 feet, must be within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.J). Specify meter specifications (single-phase, three-phase, main vs. sub-meter).

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 meter locations on building exterior walls and 4 transformer pad locations distributed across the site. Meters appear to be positioned on various building sides (north, west, south, east). Transformers are located in northwest, southwest, northeast, and southeast areas. Without clear sight line diagrams, elevation views, or explicit distance callouts, it is not possible to verify that all 8 meters are within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The term "within sight" in UCM § 1.9.3.1.B does not specify a distance limit (older references to "150 ft line of sight" are not codified), but direct visual contact must be apparent. Given the distributed meter and transformer locations, several meters may not have clear line-of-sight to a transformer.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1.B requires meters to be within sight of an Austin Energy transformer. The grouping notes that "within sight" visibility is the current code requirement with no maximum distance specified, but direct visual contact is required. Without sight line diagrams showing clear, unobstructed lines between each meter and its serving transformer, the reviewer cannot confirm compliance. The scattered distribution of transformers and meters across 8 buildings suggests that some meters may be obstructed by building walls or other structures, requiring line-of-sight verification or AE Design approval for exceptions.
findings.comment: Meter sight line to transformer not verified. Show on the electrical plan or a separate diagram that each electrical meter is within clear sight line of its serving transformer. If any meter does not have direct line of sight to the nearest transformer, provide written approval from Austin Energy Design and Distribution Metering business units for the exception. Provide sight line diagrams or cross-reference elevation views confirming visibility.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electrical routing, transformer pads, and meter locations, but does not explicitly identify or label a point-of-service (POS) location. UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as the location where Austin Energy's conductors connect with the customer's conductors. The plan shows meters on building walls and transformers in common areas but does not label the specific location(s) where the connection point(s) between AE and customer infrastructure occur. No callout identifies the meter socket, pedestal, service distribution enclosure, pull box, or other location where the POS connection is made.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines point of service as a critical infrastructure element. The POS location must be clearly identified because it designates the boundary between Austin Energy responsibility (up to the POS) and customer responsibility (from the POS onward). Without explicit POS identification, the reviewer cannot verify that the service configuration is properly documented, that customer conductors are correctly routed, and that Austin Energy access to the service point is protected. For multi-unit developments, the POS is especially important for understanding service distribution, metering grouping, and disconnect coordination.
findings.comment: Point-of-service location not shown. Identify and label the point-of-service (POS) location(s) where Austin Energy conductors connect to customer conductors. This may be at a meter socket, pedestal, SDE (service distribution enclosure), pull box, or other approved enclosure. Label with "Point of Service" notation and specify the type of enclosure. Verify that all customer conductors originate from the labeled POS.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows "Underground Electric Line" routing from the west property edge, through pull boxes, to transformers and meter locations. The underground line enters the site from the left (west) boundary and is drawn as a continuous blue line. However, the plan does not explicitly label: (1) where the service stub originates or enters the site, (2) the specific point of service where AE and customer conductors connect, (3) the direction of conductor flow from the POS to transformers and meters. The routing is shown but the origin point and termination points are not clearly called out.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that service conductor routing be clearly shown from point of service to AE facilities (transformer). The current documentation shows the routing line but lacks explicit identification of the POS location and the service stub entry point. This creates ambiguity: it is unclear whether the line entering from the west represents a service drop from overhead AE lines, an underground service stub from an AE duct bank, or another configuration. Without explicit callouts identifying the POS and service origin, Austin Energy cannot confirm that customer conductors are properly sized, protected, and routed.
findings.comment: Service conductors from point of service to AE facilities not clearly identified. Label the point where the underground service stub enters the site and the point of service connection (where AE and customer conductors meet). Show the routing clearly with callouts identifying: (1) service entry point from AE (duct bank, pole, or underground source), (2) point of service location, (3) service distribution enclosure (SDE) or main disconnect location, (4) direction of conductor flow to transformers and meter banks. Verify that service conductors are protected per code and sized per load calculations.
